localChanges: The 500 ms tick toggled the active-unit layer and composited all eleven visible layers unconditionally. With no active unit that layer draws nothing, so the toggle was invisible and the composite was pure waste twice a second (#45). It now skips both, and still drains any pending tiles and composites when it had tiles to build. `renderActiveUnit` sets the layer visible again whenever a unit becomes active, so leaving the flag untouched is safe.

`ActiveUnit.render()` also inherited `Map.clear()`, wiping the entire layer canvas -- 2560x1920 here -- to draw one 32px tile. It now clears only the region it last drew, which measures as a single 34x34 clear (tile plus the stacked-unit offset) where there was previously a full-canvas one.

Verified in the browser against a real asset import: the blink still runs at exactly one composite per 500 ms while a unit is active, the unit's terrain is cleanly restored on each off-phase, and moving the active unit leaves no trail at the tiles it came from.
